story_ai.headline: Indian markets face a soft start as global yields rise and GIFT Nifty signals a gap-down opening.
paragraphs: GIFT Nifty is at 25200, indicating a gap-down opening of approximately 99.3 points for the Nifty 50 compared to its last close of 25299.4. This follows a session where the Nifty gained 0.2% and the Bank Nifty rose 1.2%, while the India VIX cooled off by 5.4% to 16.6.

Global markets were largely subdued overnight. US indices including the S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Dow Jones all closed lower by roughly 0.4%. However, US futures are showing a modest recovery this morning. In Asia, the Nikkei 225 and Taiwan index are trading higher, while the Hang Seng has declined by 0.7%. European markets closed with slight gains on Tuesday.

Commodity prices show gold at 3920.7 and silver at 50.45, both trading higher. WTI crude is down 0.6% to 88.23. In currency markets, the USD/INR pair is at 94.0, while the US 10Y yield has risen by 10.5 bps to 5.1%, a move historically sensitive for emerging market flows.

FIIs have been active, having sold Rs 7831 crore in the cash market during the previous session. Options data shows the Nifty max pain at 25200, with significant call walls at 26000 and put walls at 24000, reflecting a cautious positioning as the PCR sits at 0.9.

Today is a heavy day for corporate results, with numerous companies including Eicher Motors, Grasim, RVNL, and Natco Pharma reporting. Oil India is in focus following its report of growth in crude oil production and standalone PAT. Other notable updates include board meetings for Ola Electric, Manappuram Finance, and IRCTC.
watch: Impact of the 10.5 bps rise in US 10Y yields on FII sentiment.
Price action around the 25200 level, which aligns with both the GIFT Nifty open and the Nifty max pain.
Volatility in stocks under the F&O ban, currently limited to KAYNES.
Market reaction to the high volume of quarterly results from companies like Eicher Motors and Grasim.
